uncited: Unlike transform-based methods that decorrelate data globally, this family operates locally or temporally to exploit spatial or temporal coherence directly.
It sets itself apart from its siblings by focusing on the prediction mechanism itself—whether spatial, temporal, or directional—rather than the transform domain or entropy coding scheme.
**Prediction:** The core operation generates $V_{pred}$ from a causal neighborhood (spatial) or a reference frame (temporal).
**Residual Calculation:** The residual $R = V_{actual} - V_{pred}$ is computed.
In lossless contexts, $R$ is exact; in lossy contexts, $R$ may be quantized.
Scan the pixels in eight directions for each block.
Determine the direction with minimum entropy.
Encode the difference by DPCM in the determined direction.
Calculate prediction coefficients for the determined direction.
Use DPCM only to determine the prediction direction for the original pixel.
Predictive coding has its roots in early telecommunications and image compression, where Differential Pulse Code Modulation (DPCM) was used to reduce the dynamic range of signals before quantization.
In volume rendering, it was adapted to handle the large spatial redundancy in 3D scalar fields.
More recent approaches integrate prediction into wavelet-based frameworks (e.g., RDLS-SS-DWT+Pred) to handle the high entropy of detail subbands [11251-rdls-ss-dwt-pred.md].
